title: ConfigMap: injecting configuration into a pod without rebuilding the image

videos.script: An image should be the same in every environment. The test cluster and production run the same bytes. What differs is configuration. {{same}} A ConfigMap is an object that holds that configuration: keys and values, or whole files. A pod reads it in one of two ways. As environment variables, or as files on a volume. {{two}} The two ways behave differently when the configuration changes, and that difference catches people. {{catch}} You will change both, and measure. The file follows the change on its own, after a delay you will time. The variable does not follow at all until the pod is replaced. {{measure}} Last, a ConfigMap that refuses to be changed, on purpose. {{immutable}}
